mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has trended upward consistently over four weeks (from -22.7% to -18.6%), indicating a steady recovery in consumer mobility. This monotonic improvement will continue over the next four weeks, driven by habituation and normalization of shopping behavior.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen from 1.0% to 5.0% over three weeks, signaling increased essential-goods shopping. When essential-goods mobility rises above 4%, consumers develop shopping routines that extend to adjacent retail categories, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 5.0% in t-1w and 2.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 4%, or GROCERY_PHARM drops below 2% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has remained severely depressed (range -29.3% to -31.4%), constraining access to retail districts. If TRANSIT mobility does not recover by at least 5 percentage points within one week, RETAIL_REC will decline further as commuting-dependent retail footfall remains suppressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -28% for the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point in the next week despite TRANSIT remaining below -28%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been consistently negative (range -7.6% to -11.9%), indicating suppressed outdoor leisure. When PARKS mobility is below -7%, it signals reduced discretionary outdoor activity, which redirects some consumer spending to indoor retail venues, producing a net positive effect on RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days while PARKS remains below -7%, or PARKS recovers above -5% and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility elevation (mean 18.5% over four weeks) combined with WORKPLACES depression (mean -18.1%) indicates a work-from-home regime. Under this regime, daytime retail visits shift to off-peak hours; when RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remains depressed, RETAIL_REC will decline as peak shopping windows compress.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite the RESIDENTIAL-WORKPLACES spread remaining above 30 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November in Singapore marks the onset of year-end holiday shopping season. GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC typically co-move during this period as consumers consolidate shopping trips. If GROCERY_PHARM sustains above 2%, RETAIL_REC will accelerate upward within two weeks as seasonal demand compounds.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 2.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2021-11-15, start of holiday season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 1 percentage point over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapse (averaging -30.5%) is the binding constraint on retail access. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed unless TRANSIT recovers by at least 8 percentage points within one week, signaling a policy shift enabling commuting and retail district access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by at least 8 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -29.3% in four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers by 8+ percentage points but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility volatility (range -24.4% to -15.3%) combined with sustained RESIDENTIAL elevation indicates unstable commuting patterns. When WORKPLACES fluctuates by more than 8 percentage points week-on-week, retail footfall becomes unpredictable; RETAIL_REC will decline as consumers defer discretionary shopping due to schedule uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change exceeds 8 percentage points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped 9.1 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES volatility exceeding 8 percentage points.
